text.tspan: ID
Requirement
Statement
Source
Rationale
Method
Criteria
REQ-EE-001
reqBothRoutesInOneTopology
The vehicle network shall hold the route
through a zone controller and the direct
route in one topology.
NEED-EE-001; eeTopologyStructureConcern;
eeCommandRouteExchangeConcern; scope item
eeTopologyInScope; gap
gapEEZoneRouteInVehicles
This is a design constraint on the
structure of the vehicle network. The
lifecycle decision is whether the product
line admits one zonal vehicle network as
its reference vehicle network, from a
verdict for each requirement on each
route, so both routes run in the same
topology: verdicts from two topologies
would judge two networks. The increment
takes neither route as given
(gapEEZoneRouteInVehicles). Phases 6 to 8
decide the realization of each element and
the medium of the direct link, and how the
topology relates to the platform stack and
to the vehicle network boundary of the
AAOS SDV middleware stays open
(gapEEStackAndNetworkBoundary).
inspect
Met when the inspection of the realization
that phase 8 records, and of the
configuration of each run of the run set,
shows one topology that holds both routes:
one central computer, two zone
controllers, one Ethernet backbone between
them, a CAN bus in each zone and a direct
link from the central computer to the
actuation ECU that passes no zone
controller.
REQ-EE-002
reqCommandsOnlyFromSCOREPath
The vehicle network shall take driving
commands only from the Eclipse S-CORE
path.
NEED-EE-001; assumption
asmEEScoreCommandSource;
eeCommandRouteExchangeConcern
This is a design constraint on the input
of the vehicle network. The driving
command enters the vehicle network from
the Eclipse S-CORE path of the existing
increments on the central computer
(asmEEScoreCommandSource), the only path
over which REQ-DRIVING-038 lets the
driver-assistance system give it, and a
readiness probe is to test this first. A
command that reaches the actuation ECU by
another way, such as one given straight to
the CAN bus of its zone, would let the
vehicle act while the routes carry
nothing, so the criteria hold that each
command that reaches the actuation ECU was
taken at the boundary interface. The
statement names the Eclipse S-CORE path,
so phase 9 links it to the feature
eclipseSCORE.
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs, each driving command
that reaches the actuation ECU is one that
the vehicle network took from the Eclipse
S-CORE path at its boundary interface.
REQ-EE-003
reqCommandsOnlyOnTheirRoute
The vehicle network shall carry the
driving commands of each run only through
the elements of the route of the run.
NEED-EE-001;
eeCommandRouteExchangeConcern; scope item
eeCommandRouteInScope; scenarios SC-EE-001
to SC-EE-004
This is a design constraint on the way of
the command. A verdict holds for the route
that ran: a command of a run on the direct
route that also passes a zone controller,
or one of a run through a zone controller
that also takes the direct link, would
give that verdict to a route that did not
carry the command alone. Which elements
realize each route is decided in phases 6
to 8, with the medium of the direct link.
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs, the records show each
driving command forwarded only by the
elements of the route of the run: on the
route through a zone controller, the
network side of the central computer, the
Ethernet backbone, the zone controller of
the zone of the actuation ECU and the CAN
bus of that zone; on the direct route, the
network side of the central computer and
the direct link.
REQ-EE-004
reqDeliverCommandStreamUnchanged
In each run, the vehicle network shall
deliver to the actuation ECU each driving
command that no fault affects, once, in
its order and with each part unchanged.
NEED-EE-001; eeVehicleCommandConcern;
assumption
asmEECommandFromDrivingBaseline; scenarios
SC-EE-001 to SC-EE-004
The vehicle can act on a driving command
only if the command reaches the actuation
ECU as the vehicle network took it. The
actuation ECU takes a command for valid
only when its check value holds and its
sequence count is one more than the
reference count, so a command lost,
repeated, put out of order or changed on
its way is rejected, and a lost or changed
one costs the command after it as well.
The form of the command is the one that
the driver-assistance increment fixes at
its baseline
(asmEECommandFromDrivingBaseline). Whether
it fits a CAN frame is open
(gapEEActuationEnd); however the elements
pack it, each part arrives as it was
taken. In a run with a fault, of SC-EE-003
or SC-EE-004, it holds for each command
that no fault affects, so the vehicle
network keeps carrying the stream around
the fault; REQ-EE-008 and REQ-EE-009 state
what the actuation ECU does with what
reaches it.
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs, the driving commands
that reach the actuation ECU, apart from
those that the fault of the run affects,
are the command stream without those, each
once and in its order, with each part
equal to the part that the path gave to
the boundary interface.
REQ-EE-005
reqCarryEachCommandWithin50Ms
In each run without a fault, the vehicle
network shall carry each driving command
from the boundary interface to the
actuation ECU within 50 ms of simulation
time after taking it.
NEED-EE-001; eeVehicleCommandConcern;
assumption
asmEECommandFromDrivingBaseline; scenarios
SC-EE-001 and SC-EE-002
This is a performance requirement on the
carriage of the command. The actuation ECU
takes a command for valid only when its
issue time is no more than 100 ms of
simulation time older than its arrival,
the delay limit of the actuation adapter
of the driver-assistance increment. The
vehicle network gets half of that limit,
from the boundary interface to the
actuation ECU; the other half is the share
of the path that carries the command to
the boundary interface, which a judged run
keeps. At its baseline the source gives at
most one driving command each 100 ms of
simulation time: one image of the front
camera each 100 ms, one plan per frame
with a result and one command per plan. A
command carried within 50 ms reaches the
actuation ECU before the next one is
given, so the vehicle network carries the
commands at the cadence at which they
come. A run with a fault, of SC-EE-003 or
SC-EE-004, is outside this requirement.
The limit counts on the clock of the
virtual vehicle and makes no timing claim
for a vehicle network
(asmEESoftwareTestbedStandsIn).
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs without a fault, each
driving command reaches the actuation ECU
no more than 50 ms of simulation time
after the vehicle network took it.
REQ-EE-006
reqApplyEachValidCommand
Until the stop response starts, the
vehicle network shall apply each valid
driving command at the actuation ECU.
NEED-EE-001; eeVehicleCommandConcern;
scenarios SC-EE-001 to SC-EE-004
The vehicle acts on a driving command only
when the actuation ECU applies it, at the
simulation time at which it arrives. After
a repetition the actuation ECU applies the
next valid driving command; a loss, a
corruption, the delay of the run set or a
link that goes down leaves it 200 ms or
more without one, and once more than 200
ms pass, the stop response starts (REQ-
EE-009) and no later command is applied. A
valid command that arrives more than 200
ms after the last one comes when the stop
response is due, so the criteria leave it
out even while the start of the response
is within its tolerance. The stop response
holds until the run ends, as the
standstill of REQ-DRIVING-022 does.
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs, the actuation ECU
applies each valid driving command that
reaches it before the stop response starts
and no more than 200 ms of simulation time
after the last valid driving command
before it reached the actuation ECU, or
after the run started when it is the
first, at the simulation time at which it
reaches it.
REQ-EE-007
reqPassDetectionPartsOnAsTaken
The vehicle network shall pass the
detection parts of each driving command on
to the actuation ECU at each element as
the element received them, without
computing any of them anew.
NEED-EE-002; eeCommandItemConcern; REQ-
DRIVING-039; gap gapEEActuationEnd
This is a design constraint on the
exchange items of the vehicle network.
REQ-DRIVING-039 makes the driving command
detectable by its form: its issue time
shows a delay, its sequence count a loss
or a repetition, and its check value a
corruption. That detection holds from the
boundary interface to the actuation ECU
only if no element computes a detection
part anew: a zone controller that repacks
the command from Ethernet to CAN with a
new check value, issue time or sequence
count would hide from the actuation ECU a
fault that came before it. A record shows
a detection part that changes at an
element in a run with a fault, but no test
can tell a new check value over unchanged
parts from the one taken, so the
requirement is verified by analysis of the
realization and of the records. How a zone
controller repacks the command, and
whether the command fits a CAN frame, are
decided in phases 6 to 8
(gapEEActuationEnd). The analysis rests on
the realization that phase 8 records and
makes no freedom-from-interference claim.
analyze
Met when the run set is judged and the
analysis of the realization that phase 8
records, and of the records of the runs of
SC-EE-003 of the run set, shows, for each
element of each route, that the element
passes on the issue time, the sequence
count and the check value of each driving
command as it received them and computes
none of them anew.
REQ-EE-008
reqGiveOnlyLastValidCommand
Until the stop response starts, the
vehicle network shall give the vehicle at
the actuation ECU only the steering angle
and the acceleration of the last valid
driving command that it applied.
NEED-EE-002; REQ-MW-006; REQ-DRIVING-039;
eeNetworkFaultResponseConcern; gap
gapEEActuationEnd; scenario SC-EE-003
The driver-assistance increment places at
its actuation end the share of REQ-MW-006
that is not applying a command that the
actuation rejects, and this increment puts
the actuation in the actuation ECU, so the
vehicle network holds that share: a
command that a fault has made invalid on
its way no longer stands for what its
source gave. A fault shows at the
actuation ECU in the sequence count for a
loss or a repetition, in the check value
for a corruption, and in the issue time
against the simulation time at its arrival
for a delay, by the rules of the actuation
adapter of the driver-assistance increment
(the adapter counting decision of
2026-11-18), with the arrival time set
here in place of the newest world time of
that adapter. The arrival time counts on
the clock of the virtual vehicle, which
the testbed gives every element, so
judging the age of a command needs no
newest world time at the actuation ECU,
whose inputs stay open
(gapEEActuationEnd). Nothing is applied in
place of an invalid command, so the
vehicle keeps the last valid one; an
invalid command, a neutral control in
place of one, or a value that no command
carried each breaks this requirement. A
repetition costs that one command; the
delay of the run set costs the delayed
command and those that wait behind it, and
the stop response follows (REQ-EE-009); a
loss or a corruption costs the lost or
corrupted command and the next one, which
reveals the gap. A corruption that the
check value misses is judged by its
sequence count and its issue time alone
and can make the actuation ECU reject
later valid commands as repetitions: the
bound of the check value (the check-value
bound decision of 2026-11-21 of that
increment). Which element detects and
rejects is decided in phases 6 to 8
(gapEEActuationEnd). The requirement
carries no safety claim and no claim of
freedom from interference.
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs, what the actuation ECU
gives the vehicle before the stop response
starts is the steering angle and the
acceleration of the last valid driving
command that it applied, and nothing
before it applies the first.
REQ-EE-009
reqStopResponseAfter200Ms
The vehicle network shall start the stop
response at the actuation ECU once more
than 200 ms of simulation time pass with
no valid driving command reaching the
actuation ECU.
NEED-EE-002; REQ-DRIVING-028;
eeNetworkFaultResponseConcern; gap
gapEEActuationEnd; scenarios SC-EE-003 and
SC-EE-004
This is the share of the vehicle network
in the stop response that REQ-DRIVING-028
of INC-DRIVING-001 asks and SC-EE-004
takes for a link that goes down. The
adapter of the driver-assistance increment
has no stop response, and the actuation
ECU is the last element that a command
reaches, so it gives the response itself
because it can no longer be told to. The
200 ms of simulation time and the 300 ms
of the criteria are those of REQ-
DRIVING-028, whose rationale counts a
command every 100 ms, so that two missed
commands mean that the path has stopped;
the source of this increment gives at most
one each 100 ms. Set here: a command that
reaches the actuation ECU exactly 200 ms
after the last valid one still counts, and
the stop response starts only after that,
because a judged run without a fault can
leave exactly 200 ms between two valid
commands, and a start at 200 ms would make
the verdict of such a run depend on the
step of the clock of the testbed. Set here
too: with the rules of the actuation
adapter of the driver-assistance increment
kept, one lost or corrupted command costs
two, although REQ-DRIVING-028 reads two
missed commands as a stopped path. The
valid commands on either side of the gap
then have issue times 300 ms apart, so
more than 200 ms pass at the actuation ECU
without a valid command and the stop
response starts, unless the valid command
before the gap takes the whole 100 ms to
reach the actuation ECU and the one after
it none, which leaves exactly 200 ms and
no stop response due. Set here too: a run
ends 100 ms of simulation time after the
path gives its last driving command, more
than the 50 ms share of the vehicle
network, so that the last command can
reach the actuation ECU within the run,
and less than the 200 ms after which the
stop response starts, so that a run
without a fault ends without it. A
repetition costs only its copy. A delay
that only just makes a command late would
leave exactly 200 ms without a valid one,
where the outcome would depend on the
clock of the testbed, so the run set
delays the command by 300 ms; with the
commands that wait behind it, that leaves
more than 200 ms without a valid one on
every clock, and the stop response
follows. The stop response gives the
deceleration of REQ-DRIVING-020 with the
steering of REQ-DRIVING-021 until the run
ends, which holds the vehicle at
standstill as REQ-DRIVING-022 does, so
that it needs no vehicle speed at the
actuation ECU, whose inputs stay open
(gapEEActuationEnd). When the actuation
ECU has applied no valid command, there is
no steering angle to hold, so the stop
response gives 0°, which steers the
vehicle neither left nor right. The
response is shown on the virtual vehicle
and carries no safety claim; its time
limit counts on the clock of the virtual
vehicle and makes no timing claim for a
vehicle network.
test
Met when the run set is judged and, in
each of its runs in which more than 200 ms
of simulation time pass with no valid
driving command reaching the actuation
ECU, the actuation ECU gives the vehicle
the stop response, with its deceleration
and its steering angle, from later than
200 ms and no later than 300 ms of
simulation time after the last valid
driving command reached it, or after the
run started when none did, until the run
ends, and applies no driving command that
reaches it after those 200 ms; and when no
run of the run set holds a start of the
stop response at another time.
REQ-EE-010
reqRecordNetworkIdentity
The vehicle network shall record its
network identity before it takes the first
driving command of each run.
NEED-EE-003; eeRouteVerdictConcern; scope
item eeVerdictEvidenceInScope; scenarios
SC-EE-001 to SC-EE-004
A verdict holds only for the route, the
topology and the revision of the vehicle
network that ran, and another engineer can
rerun a run only from what it names. The
commit names the revision, and the
recorded difference tells a build with a
change that the commit lacks apart from
it, as the candidate identity of REQ-
DRIVING-044 does; the SHA-256 of each file
of the configuration and the settings read
from outside a file pin what the vehicle
network read, because a run can read what
the commit does not fix, and the files
that set the topology pin it. The recorded
command stream, its binding to the
revision that made it and the testbed
belong to System 2 and are bound there
(gapEERecordedCommandStream,
asmEESoftwareTestbedStandsIn), so the
record covers only what the vehicle
network itself runs. Phase 8 names the
files of the configuration
(gapEEBenchPlatform).
test
Met when each run of the run set has the
record before the vehicle network takes
its first driving command; when its route
is the route that the records show the
commands of the run passing; when the
named files are the files of the
configuration that phase 8 names; and when
another engineer who checks out the named
commit, applies the recorded difference
and hashes the named files obtains the
recorded values.
